intro: Voting decided who holds office. What those officials do with it depends on what happens next: who organizes workplaces and neighborhoods, who shows up at their offices, who runs next time, and who watches the money.

This page has two parts. The first explains how power gets built, using the main theories and the 2026 results. The second is a directory of 149 groups, trainings and tools from across the political spectrum, each labeled for how well we could check it.
how_to_read: Each entry says what the group does, how you can take part, its legal form, and where it sits politically. Only gifts to 501(c)(3) charities are tax-deductible; gifts to 501(c)(4)s, 527s, PACs, parties and trade associations are not. “Confirmed” means the group’s own page, or an official record, was opened on the date shown and matches the entry; it does not confirm every legal or financial detail, which the entry marks separately. “Reported in 2026 sources” means an official or dated public page showed up in search results, but we could not open it, so descriptions are brief and legal details are marked not confirmed. “Not confirmed” means we could not establish current activity or a key fact.

data_centers.title: Data centers and your power bill
data_centers.lede: This was a top-versus-bottom fight in 2026, and it is being won locally.

points.text: On Nov. 3, voters favored limits on data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures.
In Congress, the House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340) 417–3 on Sept. 16; it only asks state regulators to consider making 100 MW+ data centers pay the full cost of grid upgrades.
In the Senate, Sen. Martin Heinrich blocked fast-track passage as too weak, and a Sept. 30 motion to proceed failed 57–43, short of the 60 needed.
The binding decisions sit with your state utility commission and local zoning board: file comments in large-load tariff cases and ask new governors and legislators for a mandatory standard.

data_centers.note: A separate Senate resolution, S.Con.Res. 30, only praises the White House’s voluntary pledge.
